llm.summary: The skill is a coherent household repair assistant, but it needs Review because it can give detailed safety-critical DIY repair steps and generate unescaped HTML reports.

dimensions.detail: Optional web search for parts, videos, and local repair shops is purpose-aligned, but the optional HTML report workflow tells the agent to replace placeholders directly and save the file without requiring HTML escaping or sanitization.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains Markdown skill and reference files only, with no executable install script, dependency fetch, remote payload retrieval, or nonempty install metadata.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Activation phrases such as fix, broken, not working, how to fix, and broad Chinese equivalents are likely to trigger outside clearly scoped household repair situations; the body and report template are Chinese-only despite an English manifest description, which can reduce clarity for safety warnings.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no evidence of credential access, session/profile use, background workers, memory changes, privilege escalation, or durable system persistence; the only durable output described is an optional user-requested HTML report saved to the working directory.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The repair-assistant purpose matches the diagnostic workflow, checklists, safety warnings, and cost estimates, but the referenced guidance includes DIY steps for mains electrical work, appliance internals, and brake-related repairs that are not consistently limited to qualified professionals.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use it as general guidance only, keep hazardous work such as mains electrical, gas, microwave high-voltage, and brake-related repairs to qualified professionals unless you are properly trained, and prefer plain-text reports or sanitized HTML for any saved repair report.
llm.findings:
[YR4] unexpected: I did not find MCP/tool metadata poisoning, exploit instructions, or tool spoofing in SKILL.md; the match appears tied to manifest text rather than artifact-backed malicious behavior.
[SQP-1] expected: Repair-related activation is expected, but the artifact-backed trigger terms are very broad and can route ambiguous requests into a safety-sensitive repair workflow.
[SQP-2] expected: Detailed repair guidance is expected for this skill, but references include mains switch/outlet replacement, appliance internal part replacement, and bike/e-bike brake repair guidance with incomplete professional-only boundaries.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese repair content is coherent with the Chinese skill body, but the English manifest plus Chinese-only instructions and zh-CN HTML template create a real safety-clarity issue for non-Chinese users.
[AE4] unexpected: I checked for common zero-width and bidirectional control characters and reviewed safety-guide.md; I did not find artifact-backed evasion or hidden instructions.
[T09] unexpected: The HTML report template directly interpolates user-derived placeholders and instructs saving the generated HTML, so the scanner's HTML-injection concern is supported by the artifact even though it does not show OS-level compromise or persistence.
